# M12 scope: under `logos test` the capabilities audit never blames the
# generated test main, the standard library, or the main module; it still
# blames a third-party dependency a test reaches.
#
# RED expectation: the linker derived a symbol's package by cutting its name
# at the last '.', so any symbol with dots after the package got a bogus
# package: main..stmp_N (the tests table of _testmain.go, on every chain to
# a test function) became "main.", closures and funcvals became
# "flag.init" or "os_test.TestSpliceFile", a value-receiver method became
# "example.com/edep.T". Case A failed with
#   ERROR [capabilities::unauthorized_cgo]: Transitive dependency 'main.' reaches ...
# and cases B, C, E, and G failed the same way; case F failed on the
# escaped %2e of the dotted import path. A later regression blamed the
# same main for net.sysSocket in bufio's test binary, and blamed
# type:noalg.struct { F uintptr; R reflect ... } (a type descriptor the
# deadcode pass kept for internal/buildcfg.init) for os.StartProcess in
# crypto's test binary, so Case A builds both too.
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

# Case A: standard-library test binaries link clean. os/exec reaches
# os.startProcess, net reaches net.sysSocket and (with cgo) runtime.cgocall,
# reflect reaches reflect.ValueOf; the whole standard library is exempt.
# bufio's test reaches net.sysSocket through net_test, and crypto's test
# binary carries internal/buildcfg.init with type descriptors, exercising
# the exact shapes of both regressions.
logos test -short -run=^$ os/exec net reflect bufio crypto
stdout 'ok\s+os/exec'
stdout 'ok\s+net\s'
stdout 'ok\s+reflect'
stdout 'ok\s+bufio\s'
stdout 'ok\s+crypto\s'
! stderr 'capabilities::'
! stdout 'capabilities::'
! stdout 'FAIL'

# Case B: a Go main module's own test reaches exec, net, and cgo through
# first-party code, including closures in the module's root package:
# first-party and standard-library frames never blame.
cd b/main
logos test -short ./...
stdout 'ok\s+example\.com/bmain\s'
stdout 'ok\s+example\.com/bmain/runner'
! stderr 'capabilities::'
! stdout 'capabilities::'
cd ../..

# Case C: the same holds for a loGo/s main module.
cd c/main
logos test -short ./...
stdout 'ok\s+example\.com/cmain/run'
! stderr 'capabilities::'
! stdout 'capabilities::'
cd ../..

# Case D: a test that reaches a sink through a third-party dependency still
# fails, blamed on that dependency and never on the test main.
cd d/main
! logos test -short ./...
stderr 'ERROR \[capabilities::unauthorized_exec\]: Transitive dependency ''example\.com/ddep'' reaches ''os\.startProcess'''
stderr 'example\.com/ddep\.Init\(\)'
! stderr 'Transitive dependency ''main'
! stderr 'Transitive dependency ''example\.com/dmain'
cd ../..

# Case E: a dependency reaching exec through a value-receiver method and a
# closure is blamed under its import path, so an allowlist glob for it
# applies. The dependency is blamed as 'example.com/edep', never as
# 'example.com/edep.Runner' or 'example.com/edep.Runner.Run'.
cd e/deny
! logos test -short ./...
stderr 'ERROR \[capabilities::unauthorized_exec\]: Transitive dependency ''example\.com/edep'' reaches ''os\.startProcess'''
cd ../..
cd e/allow
logos test -short ./...
stdout 'ok\s+example\.com/eallow/app'
! stderr 'capabilities::'
! stdout 'capabilities::'
cd ../..

# Case F: a dependency whose import path has a dot in its last element
# (the linker writes %2e) is blamed and allowlisted under the real path.
cd f/deny
! logos test -short ./...
stderr 'ERROR \[capabilities::unauthorized_exec\]: Transitive dependency ''example\.com/f\.dep'' reaches ''os\.startProcess'''
cd ../..
cd f/allow
logos test -short ./...
stdout 'ok\s+example\.com/fallow/app'
! stderr 'capabilities::'
! stdout 'capabilities::'
cd ../..

# Case G: a main module whose path has a dot in its last element is
# first-party: its own test reaches exec and is never blamed.
cd g/main
logos test -short ./...
stdout 'ok\s+example\.com/g\.main/app'
! stderr 'capabilities::'
! stdout 'capabilities::'
cd ../..

# Case H: a third-party dependency's external test package keeps its
# third-party blame: the foo_test package of a dependency that reaches exec
# fails the audit, never exempted by the suffix the standard library's own
# external tests carry.
cd h/main
! logos test -short example.com/hdep
stderr 'ERROR \[capabilities::unauthorized_exec\]: Transitive dependency ''example\.com/hdep_test'' reaches ''os\.startProcess'''
cd ../..

-- b/main/go.mod --
module example.com/bmain

go 1.27

-- b/main/bmain.go --
package bmain

import "os/exec"

func Spawn() error {
	run := func() error { return exec.Command("true").Run() }
	return run()
}

-- b/main/bmain_test.go --
package bmain

import "testing"

func TestSpawn(t *testing.T) {
	if testing.Short() {
		t.Skip("reachability only")
	}
	t.Run("spawn", func(t *testing.T) { _ = Spawn() })
}

-- b/main/runner/runner.go --
package runner

import (
	"net"
	"os/exec"
)

func Run() error { return exec.Command("true").Run() }

func Dial() error {
	c, err := net.Dial("tcp", "127.0.0.1:1")
	if c != nil {
		c.Close()
	}
	return err
}

-- b/main/runner/runner_test.go --
package runner

import "testing"

func TestRun(t *testing.T) {
	if testing.Short() {
		t.Skip("reachability only")
	}
	_ = Run()
	_ = Dial()
}

-- c/main/go.mod --
module example.com/cmain

go 1.27

-- c/main/run/run.lgo --
package run

import "os/exec"

func Run() error {
	err := exec.Command("true").Run()
	return err
}

-- c/main/run/run_test.lgo --
package run

import "testing"

func TestRun(t *testing.T) {
	if testing.Short() {
		t.Skip("reachability only")
	}
	if err := Run(); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

module example.com/ddep

go 1.27

-- d/dep/dep.go --
package dep

import "os/exec"

//go:noinline
func Init() {
	cmd := exec.Command("echo", "hi")
	_ = cmd.Run()
}

-- e/dep/go.mod --
module example.com/edep

go 1.27

-- e/dep/dep.go --
package edep

import "os/exec"

type Runner struct{}

//go:noinline
func (Runner) Run() {
	f := func() { _ = exec.Command("echo", "hi").Run() }
	f()
}

	"os/exec"
	"testing"
)

		t.Skip("reachability only")
	}
	_ = exec.Command("echo", "hi").Run()
